info.bio: The Slits se forman en 1976 bajo el liderazgo de Ari Up (Arianna Foster) y con la malagueña Palmolive —Paloma Romero, todo un mito del primer punk, que después dejó el grupo para formar The Raincoats— a la batería. Viv Albertine y Tessa Pollitt sustituirían más tarde a las otras dos componentes originales, Kate Korus y Suzy Gutsy. Típico producto de la escena punk londinense, The Slits eran pura energía vaginal. Después de que The Clash invitara a The Slits a telonearles en su gira “White Riot”

own_scenes.family: Vanguardia postpunk: dub, funk y política
own_scenes.desc: Una pandilla de chicas montaraces (Ari Up, Viv Albertine, Tessa Pollitt, Palmolive) que empezó genuinamente inepta y mejoró al aprender lo básico y encontrar un groove reggae con Budgie. Tras librarse de Malcolm McLaren, graban Cut (Island, 1979) con Dennis Bovell: engranajes polirrítmicos, la guitarra rítmica de Albertine («una versión femenina de Steve Cropper») y voces que se superponen en geometrías extrañas. Canciones sobre consumismo, romance y alienación («Typical Girls», «Shoplifting», «Newtown»); la portada, Amazonas embadurnadas de barro. Forman con The Pop Group una tribu y el sello Y; «In the Beginning There Was Rhythm», influida por el primer hip hop, y Return of the Giant Slits (CBS) cierran la historia.

refs.q: Mientras que otras bandas punk decían no saber cocar, pero eran secretamente competentes
refs.para: The Slics surgió del mismo lugar caótico que The Pop Group. No obstante, a diferencia de estos últimos, las chicas de The Slics no tenían inicialmente una sección rítmica sólida que anclara la anarquía; solo el skank' subliminal más débil del mundo indicaba sus intenciones punky-reggae. Mientras que otras bandas punk decían no saber cocar, pero eran secretamente competentes, las integrantes de The Slics eran genuinamente ineptas. Algunas personas dicen que el "verdadero" sonido de The Slics es su cacofonía naif de los primeros días, ese glorioso barullo producido por un grupo de chicas que se pelean con sus instrumentos y sus cuerdas vocales y parecen estar movidas solo por el gusto de la mera desfachatez. En realidad, las integrantes de The Slics mejoraron una vez que lograron aprender algunas destrezas instrumentales básicas y cuando se consiguieron una base rítmica más firme tras la partida de su bacerisca original, Palmolive, que no podía darles el groove cipo reggae que buscaban. Para su clásico primer disco de 1979, Cut (en el que el productor Dennis Bovell también jugaría un papel crucial ayudando a la banda a convertir su alborotado bochinche en un desorden menos confuso), The Slits reclutó a Budgie, un bacerista hombre que terminaría formando parce de Siouxie and che Banshees.

refs.q: El elemento más delicioso del sonido de The Slits en Cut
refs.para: El elemento más delicioso del sonido de The Slits en Cut es esa extraña geometría que crean el choque y la superposición de las voces mientras Albertine y Pollitt tejen alrededor del canturreo estridente, levemente amargo, de Ari Up. En el tema que abre el disco, "Instant Hit", las chicas forman una redondilla de armonías aleatorias que la cantante describe como "una cosa medio 'Frere Jacques"'.2 La letra, escrita por Albertine, retrata a un muchacho extremadamente delgado que "Don't like himself very much/ 'Cos he has set bis self to self-destruct" [No se gusta demasiado a sí mismo/ Porque se ha predis-2. "Frere Jacques" es una de las canciones populares para niños más conocidas en gran parte del mundo. Aunque su origen es francés, tiene versiones en múltiples idiomas (en espa ñol, se la conoce comúnmente como "La lechuza'', "Martinillo" o "Fray Santiago"). Puede ser cantada como una melodía simple o como un canon a cuatro voces. [N. de la T.]

refs.q: La tapa de Cut replica la foto de los Hombres Barro de Papúa Nueva Guinea
refs.para: La tapa de Cut replica la foto de los Hombres Barro de Papúa Nueva Guinea que aparece en la de Y. Como las chicas de The Slits, The Pop Group también suspiraba pensando en una totalidad perdida que ellos se imaginaban había existido antes de los efectos debilitantes de la civilización. En "She Is Beyond Good and Evil", Stewart había declarado: "los valores occidentales no significan nada para ella". Durante su gira de 1979, el Animal lnstincts Tour, la entrada en escena de The Pop Group era precedida por una grabación de tambores africanos y la banda, vía una entrevista en Melody Maker, había apelado a sus fans para que trajeran tambores y silbatos a los shows y los transformasen en ceremonias tribales. En otra nota, Gareth Sager dijo que las civilizaciones occidentales estaban enfermas porque, al estar "basadas en las ciudades", se encontraban desconectadas de los ciclos naturales, mientras que en las tribus africanas la represión sencillamente no existía.

tracks.title: In the Beginning There Was Rhythm

scenes.name: Art-punk y funk-punk británico
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: Las bandas artísticas del primer punk: Wire (de Pink Flag a la desolación electrónica de 154), Colin Newman, The Fall de Mark E. Smith, los anárquicos Swell Maps, los Mekons, las Slits (primera banda punk femenina) y los australianos Birthday Party de Nick Cave. Muchos punks redescubren la esencia «salvaje» del jazz y el funk: Pop Group (Y, fusión catastrófica de primitivismo y futurismo con dub, funk y agit-prop), Rip Rig & Panic, Gang Of Four, A Certain Ratio y Wolfgang Press.

scenes.author: Javier Blánquez (ed.)
scenes.desc: El punk, el funk y el dub se entretejen: el estudio como instrumento. The Slits con Dennis Bovell, The Pop Group en Bristol y, sobre todo, Adrian Sherwood y su sello On-U Sound: New Age Steppers, African Head Charge (precursor del techno-dub) y Tackhead, banda de estudio que endureció el sonido hacia el funk industrial y politizado.

podcast.title: All-Female English Punk Pioneers
podcast.body: The Slits were an all-female English band who were contemporaries of influential punk bands like The Sex Pistols and The Clash. They served as an initial inspiration for the Riot Grrrl movement, being among the female pioneers of punk and post-punk. "That would include the slits, an all-female English band, who were contemporaries of the sex pistols in the clash."

podcast.body: Despite being "beyond horrible" at playing instruments initially, Ari Up and her three friends were overlooked for their lack of technical skill because of their "guts" and the radical nature of being an all-female band at the time, which was a direct result of punk rock's encouragement of unconventional music. "Although Ari and her three friends couldn't play a note on whatever instruments they could borrow, they didn't care. They were beyond horrible at first, but again, that was overlooked. At least they had the guts. And an all-female band? And that's just crazy."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Born at a Punk Rock Show
podcast.body: The Slits formed after meeting at a punk rock show and were known for channeling their sound through reggae, reflecting the diverse influences within early punk. "There were groups like the Slits, who were born at a punk rock show and channeled everything through reggae."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Early Career and Development
podcast.body: By 1977, The Slits were supporting The Clash on a UK tour, playing with The Buzzcocks, and associating with the Sex Pistols, even appearing on the BBC. As they continued to perform, their musical skills evolved, leading to deeper grooves and funkier rhythms. "By 1977, they were supporting a new band called the Clash on a UK tour. They played with the Buzzcocks."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Early Formation and Ari Up's Background
podcast.body: Formed in 1977, the band featured a 15-year-old singer named Ari Up, who was a "wild kid" and the heiress to a significant German publishing fortune. Her mother was a scenester, hosting various musicians like members of The Clash or progressive rock artists. "In 1977, a 15 year old wannabe singer who called herself Ari Up decided that she wanted to be a musician of this extreme variety. She was a pretty wild kid and maybe had something to do with the fact that her mother was the aress to a giant German publishing fortune."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Early Musical Development and Associations
podcast.body: In their early stages, the band members were not highly skilled instrumentalists, but their focus on expression aligned with the punk ethos. By 1977, they were supporting The Clash on a UK tour, playing with The Buzzcocks, associating with The Sex Pistols, and even appearing on the BBC. "Okay, they didn't know how to play many of their instruments, but that didn't matter."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Embrace of Reggae
podcast.body: Ari Up developed a taste for reggae in 1977, which was a radical choice at the time, but reggae's influence was growing due to Jamaican immigration to Britain, fostering a mixing of cultures and music. "Ari developed a taste for reggae. And this is more radical than it sounds right now. See today, reggae and scott, that's everywhere, right? Not so in 1977, but that was changing thanks to the political and economic situation in Jamaica."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Evolving Sound Towards Funk
podcast.body: As The Slits continued to play, their musical abilities grew, leading to deeper grooves and more funky rhythms in their sound. This evolution showcased their development beyond the raw energy of early punk. "And the more they played, the better they got. The grooves got deeper and the rhythms more funky."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Formation and Punk Ethos
podcast.body: The Slits were formed by four teenage women in London after repeatedly encountering each other at early punk shows. Despite their initial lack of musical proficiency, their primary focus was on self-expression and the courage to articulate their ideas, embodying the core principles of punk rock. "Four teenage women who decided to form a band after seeing each other again and again and again at early punk shows around London. They decided to form their own band."

podcast.title: Punk Pioneers
podcast.body: Members of The Slits were pioneers who embraced punk rock values, contributing to the movement's ethos of self-expression irrespective of gender or background. "Suzy Su, of Suzy in the Banshee's, members of the Slitz, Pauli Styrene of X-Ray Specks, Chrissy Hinder, the Pretenders, Patty Smith, and so many more. They were all pioneers and they all inspired many people, women, but also men, to do what they did."

xref.title: First Gig (November 1975)
xref.body: The Sex Pistols played their first gig in November 1975, the same month Patti Smith released her influential debut album "Horses." They were contemporaries of The Slits and a foundational band of the punk movement. "That was the same month the sex pistols played their first gig"

xref.title: Contemporaries of The Slits
xref.body: The Clash were contemporaries of The Slits, an all-female English punk band that served as an inspiration for the Riot Grrrl movement. They were part of the same original punk rock scene in England. "who were contemporaries of the sex pistols in the clash."

xref.title: Contribution to The Slits and The Raincoats
xref.body: Although Paloma Romero (Palmolive) did not appear on any records by The Slits after leaving the band, several of her songs were used. She then moved on to join The Raincoats, another influential all-female punk band highly praised by Kurt Cobain. "Palmolev never appeared on any slits records. She'd quit the band by then, but several of her songs were used. Instead, she moved on and joined the raincoats, another all-female band, and one of Kurt Cobain's all-time favorite groups."

srcs.episode: Driven By Her: History of Female Drummers

xref.title: Early Punk Drummer and Quick Learning
xref.body: Paloma Romero, a Spanish-born drummer, became a key figure in the early UK punk scene. Inspired by the movement, she learned to play drums in just one week before joining The Slits, an all-female band she co-founded with two 14-year-olds. "The whole scene inspired her to learn how to play the drums. She says she practiced for a whole week to learn how to play them. And then she joined an all-female band with a couple of 14-year-olds and they became the slits."

xref.title: Johnny Rotten's Secret Wealth – Married to Publishing Heiress Worth ~£50 Million; Made Millions in UK Real Estate
xref.body: Despite assiduously maintaining his working-class punk image, John Lydon is married to Nora Forster, a German media and publishing heiress with an estimated net worth of approximately £50 million. They met during the Pistols' original run in the late 1970s when Lydon was about 22 and Forster was 36. Nora's daughter from a previous relationship was Ari Up, singer of The Slits — meaning Ari introduced her mother to Johnny. Additionally, unbeknownst to most punk fans, Lydon has made a considerable personal fortune by investing in the UK real estate market. "Johnny Rotten, punk by profession but secretly very, very comfortable."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Kim Gordon's Diverse Inspirations
xref.body: Kim Gordon drew inspiration from a wide range of female artists across different genres, including punk icons like Patty Smith and the Slits, Goths like Suzy Su, rockers like Joan Jett and The Runaways, blues singers like Billie Holiday, and her ultimate heroine, Tina Turner. "She was inspired by the women who came before her. There were punks like Patty Smith and the slits, Goths like Suzy Su, Rockers like Joan Jaden, The Runaways, Blues singers like Billie Holiday, and her greatest heroine, Tina Turner."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Reggae and Diverse Influences
xref.body: The band was open to new ideas, particularly the reggae sounds emanating from the apartments of new immigrants in Britain. Their appreciation for reggae led them to explore ska, blues, R&B, soul, and rockabilly, incorporating these into their music. "But like the teenagers in the Slits, they were open to all kinds of new ideas, especially the new reggae sounds that were being played out of the windows of the apartments where the new immigrants lived."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Relationship Origin with Nora
xref.body: Johnny met his wife Nora through her daughter, Ari. In the 1970s, Ari was in the punk band The Slits and moved in the same circles as the Sex Pistols, becoming friends with Johnny. "Johnny met Nora through Ari. Back in the 1970s, Ari was in a punk band called The Slits."
